title: Nothing builds the site before a merge, so only a Liquid brace is caught in time

evidence.verified: `npm run pages:build` exits 0 on this tree in 1.7 seconds. Reverted against the documents as they stood at c2711c1~1, in a throwaway worktree, it exits 1 and names the cause: `Liquid syntax error (line 275): Variable '{{ width: "100%"...' was not properly terminated`. So the gate can fail, which is the thing a new gate has to prove. `npm run ci` exits 0 at 1244860 reporting `every gate ran`, and with both container runtimes forced absent it still exits 0 while reporting `2 gate(s) did not run` and naming the site build among them. `actionlint` exits 0 on the changed workflows.

details:
`pages.yml` runs on a push to `main` and nowhere else, so the site is first built after the merge. CUI-073 is what that cost once: eleven Liquid braces reached `main`, and the build reported them to whoever merged.

Section 9 of `check-integrity.mjs` now catches that one failure mode before the commit exists. It does not build the site. A change to `_config.yml`, a document that gains a YAML header, or anything else Jekyll refuses still reaches `main` before anyone hears about it.

Building on a branch is cheap. The `github-pages` gem, version 232, builds this tree in a container in about a second with `PAGES_REPO_NWO` set. It fails on the documents as they stood at c2711c1~1 and passes on them as they stand now. A build job in `ci.yml` using `actions/jekyll-build-pages@v1`, with no deploy job after it, would cover every push.

The cost is the mirror. CONTRIBUTING says `npm run ci` is every gate the workflow has, in the order the workflow takes them, so a job with no local counterpart weakens that sentence. A local counterpart needs Ruby, which nothing else here needs, and a gate that skips where Ruby is missing is the shape of hole this record is about.

notes.text:
The cost this record weighed turned out not to be real, which is why it closes with a local mirror rather than without one.

The objection recorded above was that a local counterpart needs Ruby, and that a gate skipping where Ruby is missing is the shape of hole this record describes. It needs no Ruby. The gate runs `actions/jekyll-build-pages`' own image, so its only prerequisite is a container runtime, which is what the visual gate already asks for. `npm run ci` names the skip on the way out, as it already does for that gate and for `actionlint`.

The gem is version 232 and the build takes under two seconds, so nothing about the run is expensive enough to argue about.
